# Harden proxy start against foreground invocation being killed by tool-call timeouts

## Problem statement

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` ends with `exec "$PY_BIN" -m uvicorn proxy.server:app …`, so the
server runs inside whatever process group launched the script. When an agent runs the script in the
foreground under a bash tool call, the harness's tool timeout (60 s) SIGKILLs the whole process
group, killing uvicorn mid-startup with no `Shutting down` line — and because the same invocation
passed `--restart` (which had already SIGTERM'd the previous instance), the proxy is left
completely offline with no error surfacing anywhere except the tool result.

Observed once on 2026-10-20 (session `herdr-1792503008-530778-31323`, tool result
`Command timed out after 60 seconds`). llama-server (preserved by the restart gate) and TTS
(spawned via `nohup` inside the proxy) survived; only the foreground uvicorn died.

## Users and user stories

- **Agent session running a start/restart** — "As an agent asked to restart the proxy, I want the
  server to keep running after my tool call ends or times out, so that a restart never leaves the
  service dead."
- **Operator debugging the proxy** — "As an operator, I sometimes want to watch the server in the
  foreground; I want that to be an explicit opt-in so I cannot do it by accident."
- **Future on-call session** — "As an agent diagnosing a dead proxy, I want a documented signature
  that tells me this failure happened in seconds, so that I restart correctly instead of
  re-investigating."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Server survives the launcher's process-group death.** By default
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` performs all of its synchronous validation (port free, provider API
  keys resolved, config readable, restart/cleanup phases) and then launches uvicorn in its **own**
  session/process group (`setsid`, with a `nohup … &` + `disown` fallback when `setsid` is
  unavailable), redirecting the child's stdout/stderr to a log file (`--log-file <path>`, default
  `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`) so the caller's pipe is **not** held open. It prints a single handoff
  line (child PID, log path, health-check command) and exits 0.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit foreground opt-in.** `--foreground` (or `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` for
  unattended callers that cannot pass flags) keeps today's blocking `exec` behaviour for interactive
  debugging. The flag is parsed and consumed by the script (never forwarded to uvicorn) and is
  documented in the usage header. Without it, foreground execution is not possible.
- [ ] **AC3 — Regression test for the failure mode.** A test asserts the launched server survives
  `SIGKILL` of the launching shell's entire process group: it starts the script in its own pgid,
  waits until the fake server binds an ephemeral port, `kill -9 -<launcher-pgid>`, then asserts the
  listener still answers. Sandboxed per the existing pattern (copy of the script, fake `python3`
  that stands in for uvicorn, isolated `$HOME`, stubbed `ss`/`netstat`, ephemeral port) so the live
  proxy, port 8000, llama-server and TTS are never touched, and it runs in the default suite.
- [ ] **AC4 — Docs: never start in the foreground under an agent tool call.**
  `/skill:start-proxy` (`.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`) and `proxy/README.md` state explicitly,
  in the start/restart section, that the proxy must never be started in the foreground under an
  agent tool call and show the exact detached command to use, plus the `--foreground` escape hatch
  and its `--log-file` companion.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs: diagnostic signature.** Documentation lists the signature of this failure so a
  future session recognises it immediately: proxy log ends abruptly with **no `Shutting down`
  line**, the triggering tool result reads `Command timed out after <N> seconds`, the launcher was
  run in the foreground, and sibling services (llama-server/TTS) are still alive. It also records
  the correct recovery (`/skill:start-proxy --restart`, warm llama-server preserved).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing callers and harnesses unaffected.** The already-detached call patterns
  (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &` in the skill and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh`, and `--restart`'s `pkill`/port-release logic) keep working,
  and the existing shell harnesses (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`,
  `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh`,
  `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh`) are updated with `--foreground` where they
  intentionally intercept the final `exec`, or otherwise still pass.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including script
  comments, `proxy/README.md`, the start-proxy skill, and any relevant runbook entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the uvicorn command line, config resolution, API-key fail-closed behaviour, restart
  gate or `--keep-llama-server` semantics — this is a launch-harness change only.
- Detaching must **not** inherit the caller's stdout/stderr pipe: inheriting it means `… | tail -20`
  still blocks the tool call until timeout and re-creates the original failure.
- Startup failures after the handoff (bind errors, model load failures, import errors) can no longer
  be reported through the launcher's exit code; callers must poll `/health`. The start-proxy skill
  already does this, and the handoff line must point at the log for the failure text.
- `setsid` and `nohup` must both be tolerated; no new dependency beyond coreutils.
- Tests must never touch the live proxy, ports 8000/8080/8081, or kill unrelated processes
  (project rule: never blanket-kill `python3`/`uvicorn`).

## Existing state

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` parses `--restart`, `--reason`, `--keep-llama-server`, `--verbose`,
  `--use-env-keys`, `--port`, does all validation, then `exec`s uvicorn inline — no detach, no
  `--foreground`, no log-file option, no PID file.
- Callers already background it externally: `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`
  (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &`) and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh:77`. Nothing prevents a foreground run, and
  `proxy/README.md` §Verbose documents `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --verbose` as the
  "recommended" invocation (a foreground command) without any warning.
- Sandboxed shell-test harness pattern already exists
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`): script copy + fake `python3`
  intercepting `-m uvicorn` + isolated `$HOME` + stubbed port probes + ephemeral port. The detach
  test can reuse it.
- Related history: backgrounded starts were killed in an earlier investigation
  (LP-0MQIWGJ6L000SA29) but that root cause was the test host, not a tool timeout.

## Desired change

1. Add `--foreground` / `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` and `--log-file <path>` to the flag parser
   (consumed, never forwarded to uvicorn).
2. Replace the final `exec` with a launch helper: after all validation, if foreground was requested,
   keep today's `exec`; otherwise `setsid` a re-execution of the same script in a child session with
   the uvicorn command, stdio redirected to the log file, then print the handoff line and exit 0.
   The re-exec must pass `--foreground` and **drop `--restart`** (the kill/cleanup and port-release
   phases already ran in the launcher) so the child cannot re-enter the detach path or repeat the
   restart storm.
3. New sandboxed detach test (AC3) plus harness updates for `--foreground` where needed.
4. Documentation: skill + README foreground warning, exact detached command, and the failure
   signature/recovery entry.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — flag parsing (`--foreground`, `--log-file`,
  `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND`), detach wrapper around the final exec, handoff line, usage header.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` — **new** AC3 regression test (pgid SIGKILL survival,
  sandboxed, fake uvicorn that binds an ephemeral port and records its pid/pgid).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` — add `--foreground` to invocations that intercept the final exec.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — never-foreground warning, exact detached command,
  `--log-file`, failure signature + recovery row in the Errors table.
- `proxy/README.md` — start section, §Verbose invocation guidance, diagnostic signature.

## Related work

- **LP-0MQMC3RQ1000ZY4M** — *Hardening: start-proxy.sh and proxy startup failures* (completed): the
  same script's interpreter/port/PYTHONPATH hardening; this item is the next robustness gap in the
  same launch path.
- **LP-0MQIWGJ6L000SA29** — *Investigate proxyctl restart integration flakiness (background start
  killed)* (completed): backgrounded starts killed in the **test host**; distinct root cause, but
  it established the `nohup`/`setsid` reasoning and the sandboxed harness habit re-used here.
- **LP-0MVD2RF7H008B7OT / LP-0MVF7DRMK001NHT8** — stale-key detection + its shell tests: the
  harness whose fake-`python3` interception the detach test re-uses and which needs `--foreground`.
- **LP-0MVJX7NGN006S74K** — *llama-server restart signature ignores models.ini and start-llama.sh
  changes* (open, unrelated area, same script): touch points overlap in `start-proxy.sh`; implement
  sequentially to avoid conflicting edits.
- **LP-0MNSRGEQW000QM7B / LP-0MPY3DG43009V6LO** — proxyctl start/restart CLI (completed): the
  external wrapper that already backgrounds the script; the new default must not double-detach-break
  it.

Potentially related docs:
- `proxy/README.md` (§Verbose, §Production/start) — documents the foreground invocation that this
  item must stop recommending.
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — the canonical agent start/restart procedure.
- `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh` — already-detached caller to regression-check.
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md` and `proxy/scripts/diagnose-llama-proxy-startup.sh` — existing
  diagnosis surfaces that could host the failure signature.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: silent startup failure.** Detaching hides post-launch uvicorn failures from the exit code.
  Mitigation: keep every existing pre-launch validation synchronous, print the log path in the
  handoff line, and document health polling (already the skill's contract).
- **Risk: pipe inheritance re-creates the bug.** If the detached child keeps the caller's stdout,
  `… | tail -20` blocks until the tool timeout again. Mitigation: AC1 mandates redirecting child
  stdio to the log file.
- **Risk: harness churn.** Sandboxed shell tests assert on the intercepted exec's stdout; they need
  `--foreground`. Mitigation: AC6 keeps them green (behaviour change is explicit, not silent).
- **Risk: child re-enters the detach path or repeats `--restart`.** A naive re-exec of the same
  argv would detach again (or sleep through the restart phases a second time). Mitigation: the
  re-exec is generated explicitly with `--foreground` and without `--restart`, plus a regression
  assertion in the detach test that the fake server is launched exactly once.
- **Risk: double backgrounding** (skill already uses `nohup … &` around a now self-detaching script)
  causes a stale expectation of "script still running". Mitigation: handoff line + exit 0 makes the
  new contract explicit; the skill's command is simplified.
- **Assumption:** self-detach-by-default (with `--foreground` opt-in) is preferred over
  "document-and-warn only", because it makes the failure impossible for every caller (agents, cron,
  ad-hoc shells) instead of depending on discipline. Recorded for producer confirmation.
- **Assumption:** the default log path is `/tmp/proxy-startup.log` (matches the current skill and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh` convention).
- **Scope-creep guard:** a PID file, systemd unit, or richer `proxyctl` integration are *not* in
  scope; record them as follow-up items if they surface during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (AC1 variant):** Should the script self-detach by default with an explicit `--foreground`
  opt-in, or stay foreground-only with only a documented warning? **Recommended:** self-detach by
  default — a warning cannot prevent an agent tool timeout from killing the server.
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** self-detach by default +
  `--foreground` / `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` opt-in, as specified in AC1/AC2. Source: work item
  description's AC1 explicitly permits either variant; agent selected the stronger one. Research:
  inspected all callers (`grep -rn "start-proxy" --include=*.sh --include=*.md`), all but the README
  already background it externally, so self-detaching is additive.
- **Q2 (log destination):** Where should the detached child's output go — inherit the caller's
  stdout, or a file? **Recommended:** a file (`--log-file`, default `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`).
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** a file, because inheriting the
  caller's pipe keeps `| tail -20` blocked and reproduces the original timeout. Source: incident
  evidence in the work item (the failing invocation was piped to `tail -20`).
- **Q3 (test placement/scope):** Should the pgid-survival test be opt-in (`LIVE_*` gated) or part of
  the default suite? **Recommended:** default suite, sandboxed.
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** default suite, because the harness
  pattern in `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` already isolates everything (fake interpreter, stubbed
  port probes, isolated `$HOME`, ephemeral port), so no live service is touched. Opt-in gating is
  reserved for tests that spawn/kill real OS listeners against real ports
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_restart.sh`).
- **Q4 (issue type/priority):** Item was filed as `chore`/`medium`. **Recommended:** `bug`/`high`
  (the change alters launch behaviour, and a dead proxy blocks every consumer).
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** reclassified to `bug` (the launch
  path demonstrably leaves the service dead) with `high` priority (a dead proxy blocks every
  consumer). Producer may override.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** – proxyctl: restart command (completed)
- **LP-0MQVJ76WP009QOUE** – TTS Server Lifecycle Management (completed)
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)

### Repository file matches
_No credible file matches: the automated sweep matched AC-id tokens (ac1..ac8) in a
vendored prompt-dataset fixture. The hand-curated **Related work** section above is
authoritative._

# Prefill vs decode breakdown report section

## Summary

Add a `## Prefill vs decode` section to the generated report showing slot-seconds and % of slot-time for each phase, so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes. Also update the `## Local model utilization` table with the redefined busy metric and the retained decode-only row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `Prefill vs decode` breakdown appears in the report, reporting **slot-seconds and % of slot-time** for prefill and for decode, **so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes**.
- The section reports total prefill slot-seconds and total decode slot-seconds, each as an absolute figure and as a percentage of combined slot-time that sums to 100%.
- The section includes p10/p50/p90/max for prefill and decode, with an explicit statement that these are slot-seconds (the integral of concurrency), not wall-clock.
- `## Local model utilization` shows both the new dispatch→finish busy figure and the retained decode-only row, with the definition-change note in the section header.
- The section renders gracefully when no prefill samples exist, printing a named reason and pointing at the eval-timing diagnostic rather than leaving an unattributed blank.
- Unit tests verify section content, that the percentages sum to 100%, and empty-window rendering.

## Key Files

- `scripts/reporting.py`
- `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- LP-0MVJN9H2I00116FP (union-interval busy redefinition)

# Instrument and fix the slot sidecar seed path (restored-prefix warmness never fires)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the restored-prefix credit (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) to
actually fire for sessions that resume with a persisted slot snapshot, so the
feature is measurable — and if it cannot fire for the common case, I want to
know why with instrumentation instead of silence.

## Problem statement

The ≥24 h measurement (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K, 2026-10-22) found the seeding path
made **zero contact** in a 54.4 h post-deploy window:

- 0 `slot_ratio_restored` events, 0 `cache_state=restored` lines;
- the sidecar writer is healthy: 37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars
  written (2026-10-20 13:27 → 2026-10-22 19:43), names match the reader's
  candidate layout (`slot-cache/localhost-8080/`);
- 33 sessions with sidecars reached the local routing gate 2,918 times after
  their sidecar existed (including right after proxy restarts when the in-memory
  ratio was empty) and were still scored `cache_state=cold` — e.g. session
  `herdr-1792667491-…` (sidecar: 276 messages, saved 14:13) scored
  `cached_ratio=0.00 cache_state=cold messages=696` at 19:30 after a restart.

Root-cause suspects (in order of likelihood): (1) the `prefix_matches` guard
fails on real resumed conversations — first message (system prompt) regenerated
per request, and/or client-side compaction rewriting the front of the history
(proxy-side compaction is disabled: `compaction_bypass_eval … reason=compaction_disabled`);
(2) sidecars only exist for old snapshots, so a 24 h TTL plus front-rewrites
leaves no credit window; (3) (checked, unlikely) endpoint string drift between
save and seed. Seed outcomes log at DEBUG only, invisible at the INFO level the
proxy runs at.

## Split at producer request (2026-10-22)

The producer chose **instrument first**. The observability half is now its own S
child, **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** (INFO-level `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` logging +
tests + docs), and this item depends on it. Do not change the credit logic
(`prefix_matches`, the sidecar TTL, the sidecar format) until the interface has
produced one traffic cycle of outcome counts: a fix attempted without that data
is guesswork. Effort below (M) covers the remaining fix plus the ≥24 h
re-measurement; priority is medium while it waits on data.

## Proposed change

1. Using the instrumented outcome counts, decide which failure mode is real:
   too-strict `prefix_matches` (rewritten system prompt / client-compacted
   history), an expired sidecar (24 h TTL vs long-lived sessions), or a lookup
   miss. Record the decision and the supporting data on this item.
2. Fix only the confirmed cause, consistent with AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (a
   *changed* prompt still earns nothing; a *reusable prefix* must earn credit).
   Candidate approaches to evaluate: fingerprint the non-system messages only;
   anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash; credit the last-saved overlapping
   messages; or compare against the last K messages of the stored list instead
   of requiring a prefix. Re-evaluate the TTL if it is the binding constraint.
3. Add a unit test reproducing the real resume pattern (sidecar saved for a full
   conversation; resumed request arrives with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   compacted front) that fails before the fix and passes after it.
4. Re-run the ≥24 h before/after measurement with
   `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (built by LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K):
   post-fix `cache_state=restored` dispatches must be > 0, and seeded dispatches
   must beat cold dispatches in the same context bucket (sample counts +
   percentiles).
5. Document the changed guard in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written verdict on this item names the confirmed failure mode and cites the instrumented outcome counts that prove it.
- For the confirmed cause, a unit test reproduces the resume-with-rewritten-front case and fails on the pre-fix code.
- After the fix, a ≥24 h window contains `cache_state=restored` dispatches, and their `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles are stated against cold dispatches in the same context bucket with sample counts.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (mismatched snapshots earn nothing; restored ratio ≤ measured × margin).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the resolved guard and its failure modes.

## Risks / notes

- The 24 h TTL (`session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds`) may itself be too short for
  the resume pattern observed (sidecar at 276 messages, resume at 696); include
  TTL in the investigation.
- Attribution caveat: the local-prefill improvement in the measurement window
  came from other changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering); do not
  use it as evidence for this path.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (the AC5 measurement that found zero seeds)
- implementation of: LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (restored slot-prefix warmness)
- blocked by: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (seed-outcome instrumentation)
- report: docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — the seed path and its guard: `prefix_matches()`,
  `seed_cached_ratio()` (validation order: snapshot → sidecar → model → TTL → prefix),
  `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()`. The confirmed-cause fix lands here.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` applies the *same*
  `prefix_matches` guard to the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812); a guard change
  must be evaluated for both call sites, not just the sidecar.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — add the resume-with-rewritten-front
  reproducer alongside the existing guard/TTL tests.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530): document the
  resolved guard and its failure modes.
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — the AC3 re-measurement.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the baseline the
  re-measurement is compared against.

## Plan (features and implementation tasks, 2026-10-22)

The five acceptance criteria decompose into three independently deliverable
slices plus the prerequisite instrumentation, in dependency order (verification
slices before implementation, per the plan skill's test-first rule):

| # | Work item | Type | Covers | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** — Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO | task (S, risk Low) | prerequisite data (INFO `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`) | — |
| 1 | **LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3** — Diagnose the seed failure mode from outcome counts | task (verification) | AC1 | item 0 |
| 2 | **LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC** — Fix the confirmed seed guard and document it | bug (test-first slice) | AC2, AC4, AC5 | item 1 |
| 3 | **LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3** — Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix | task (verification) | AC3 | item 2 |

**Why three slices:** AC1 needs the instrumentation's outcome counts (a
traffic-cycle wait), and AC3 needs a ≥24 h post-fix window (another wait).
Neither wait can complete inside a single fix run, so each is its own item
with its own worktree lifecycle; the fix itself stays one vertical slice
(code + failing-then-passing test + docs) rather than being split
horizontally.

**Deliberately undecided:** the fix technique (non-system fingerprinting, a
stable prompt-prefix anchor, last-K overlap credit, or a TTL change) is chosen
from the diagnosis verdict, not here — the producer's "instrument first" split
stands. A fix attempted without the outcome counts is guesswork.

**Between phases:** after the diagnosis verdict lands, re-read the fix item's
description and update it so the reproducer test and the guard change match
the confirmed mode; after the fix lands, confirm the deployed build before the
re-measurement window starts.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** – Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing) (open)
- **LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K** – Measure restored slot-prefix warmness impact over >=24h (before/after) (completed)
- **LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV** – Second-turn cached_ratio scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn (bootstrap defect in update_cached_ratio) (completed)

### Repository file matches (verified by inspection)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — `prefix_matches()` (the suspected guard), `seed_cached_ratio()` validation order, `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()` (TTL), `_candidate_slot_filenames()` (lookup)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` reuses the same `prefix_matches` guard for the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812), so any guard change affects both paths; `_last_prompt_prefix` store
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — existing guard/TTL tests (`test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`, `test_expired_sidecar_earns_no_credit`, `test_ttl_zero_disables_expiry`) to extend with the resume-with-rewritten-front case
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530) to update
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — ≥24 h before/after re-measurement tool
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — baseline figures and sidecar inventory to compare against

## Intake notes (verification pass, 2026-10-22)

- **No interview required.** The seed brief already carried a problem statement with
  evidence, five measurable acceptance criteria, scoped constraints ("do not change the
  credit logic until the instrumentation has produced one traffic cycle"), risks and
  traceability; the remaining questions are answerable from the repo, which was read
  during this pass (seed path, guard, tests, docs, measurement report).
- **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search` on "slot sidecar restored prefix warmness"):
  no duplicate item exists. Related, non-overlapping items are the completed implementation
  LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304, the completed measurement LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (which triggered this
  item), the open instrumentation child LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and the completed
  expected-reuse credit LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV.
- **Assumption (recorded, not decided):** the failure mode is not chosen here. The
  producer's "instrument first" split stands — this item stays `blocked` on
  LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and its fix is selected from the instrumented outcome counts.
- **Note on the shared guard:** because `prefix_matches` is also used by
  `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` for the in-memory expected-reuse credit, any guard
  change is a two-call-site change; the AC2 unit test must therefore assert the sidecar
  path *and* confirm the expected-reuse path still refuses a genuinely changed prompt
  (AC4).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan, 2026-10-22)

**No operator questions were asked in this session.** Rationale: the intake
brief already carried the producer's "instrument first" decision, five
measurable ACs, explicit scope constraints and full traceability; the
plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (effort Medium, risk
Medium — the gate pauses only for Extra Large effort combined with High/Severe
risk), so no approval pause was warranted. Everything the plan needed was
answerable from this work item and the repository, which was read during this
session.

data.description:
## Goal

Make the `/slots` single-flight helper in `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
cancellation-safe: a leader that is cancelled (browser disconnect cancels the SSE
handler) must never orphan the shared future, and a follower must never `await`
that future without a bound. This is the core fix for parent
LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5).

## Current defect (verified)

```python
if not leader:
    return await fut                     # unbounded follower wait
except Exception as exc:                 # CancelledError is BaseException
    if not fut.done():
        fut.set_exception(exc)
    raise
finally:
    async with lock:
        _slots_poll_inflight.pop(url, None)   # owner forgotten, future PENDING
```

`asyncio.CancelledError` bypasses `except Exception`, so the future is left
pending forever while the registry entry is removed — every follower hangs, and
`_periodic_broadcast_loop()` can stall for all connected clients.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A follower awaiting an in-flight `/slots` fetch is released when the leader is cancelled (`asyncio.CancelledError`), rather than blocking forever; `_fetch_slots_payload()` resolves or cancels the shared future on that (or any `BaseException`) before re-raising, and the regression test from LP-0MVK1YCVV007HNAG passes.
- AC2: A follower never waits unboundedly — if the leader disappears without resolving the future, the follower either re-fetches as a new leader (re-registering the inflight future) or returns the last-known/cached values within its own timeout; the wait must not cancel the shared future for other followers (`asyncio.shield` / `asyncio.wait`, not a bare `wait_for(fut)`).
- AC3: Cancelling a request that owns the single-flight fetch does not leak a pending future or emit "Future exception was never retrieved" / "Task was destroyed but it is pending" warnings; LP-0MVK1YCVV007HNAG AC3 passes.
- AC4: The documented reproduction fails before the fix and passes after it, using the existing test-skill runner (no ad-hoc pytest invocations); the before/after output and the changed-scope suite result are recorded in a comment on this item.
- AC5: `_periodic_broadcast_loop()`'s follower path can no longer stall permanently — verified by trace/reasoning plus the coalescer-level tests (no new loop-level test is required).

## Approach (smallest end-to-end slice)

- Replace `except Exception` with `except BaseException` (or
  `except (Exception, asyncio.CancelledError)`) and resolve the future before
  re-raising: `if not fut.done(): fut.cancel()` is acceptable, but prefer
  setting a defensive result so followers degrade to last-known values rather
  than raising.
- Bound the follower path with the caller's own `timeout` (or a dedicated
  `SLOTS_POLL_FOLLOWER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default ≤ `timeout`) using
  `asyncio.shield`, then fall back to a fresh leader attempt / cached payload.
- Keep the `finally` cleanup: registry entry removed only when this caller still
  owns it (avoid popping a newer leader's future).
- Add a short comment block documenting the invariant (future always resolved;
  follower wait always bounded) and reference LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:295` — `_fetch_slots_payload()`: cancellation-safe future handling and bounded follower wait.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:226` — `_slots_poll_inflight` / `_slots_poll_cache` registry semantics.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:1737` — `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` follower path (the all-clients stall).
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py` — regression tests that must pass after the fix.

# Detach survival regression test harness

Test-first item for LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY (Harden proxy start against foreground
invocation being killed by tool-call timeouts). Proves (RED first) that the
launched server survives `SIGKILL` of the launcher's entire process group, and
that `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` runs in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the launched server survives `SIGKILL` of the launching shell's
  entire process group: it starts the script in its own pgid, waits until the
  fake server binds an ephemeral port, `kill -9 -<launcher-pgid>`, then asserts
  the listener still answers.
- [ ] Sandboxed per the existing pattern (copy of `start-proxy.sh`, fake `python3`
  that stands in for uvicorn and records its pid/pgid, isolated `$HOME`, stubbed
  `ss`/`netstat`, ephemeral port) so the live proxy, port 8000, llama-server and
  TTS are never touched, and no unrelated process is killed.
- [ ] The harness asserts the fake server is launched exactly once and its pgid
  differs from the launcher's (detached session, no detach re-entry); it asserts
  the launcher prints a single handoff line (child PID, log path, health-check
  command) and exits 0; it asserts the child's stdout/stderr go to the log file
  and not the caller's pipe (the caller's stdout reaches EOF promptly).
- [ ] `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` is executable and runs standalone
  (`bash tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh`), and `tests/test_start_proxy_detach_shell.py`
  is a thin pytest wrapper that runs it as a subprocess so the regression test
  executes in the default suite (precedent: `tests/test_git_hooks.py`,
  `tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py`); it skips cleanly when `bash` is
  unavailable.
- [ ] The harness exits non-zero against the current foreground-`exec` script and
  the RED run output/evidence is recorded as a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` — **new**, executable sandboxed harness.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_detach_shell.py` — **new**, thin pytest wrapper.

## Notes

- Harness pattern to mirror: `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` and
  `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`.
- Commit (RED) before the start-proxy script change is implemented.
